about: Every headline claim, its basis and whether it may be shown. GREEN: implementation and source checked. AMBER: shown only with its qualification. RED: must not appear as an established result. A unit test (frontend/src/services/claims.test.ts) fails if the wording of a RED claim appears on any live surface.

claims.claim: Real NISAR measurements of the event are loaded
claims.basis: Pair A GUNW/GOFF and Pair B GOFF COGs, each tagged with its granule ID; Provisional, CRID P05023

claims.claim: Coherence 0.19 against 0.46 (frame 74) and 0.16 against 0.52 (frame 75), inside the UNOSAT extent against a 1 km ring
claims.basis: data/qa/pair-a-analysis.json, valid-mask pixels only: 36.5% of the extent in frame 74 and 44.0% in frame 75. Recomputed from the raw files on 13 Nov, unchanged. UNOSAT's extent is preliminary and not field validated
claims.action: Keep the valid share next to the figures

claims.claim: At the source, Pair A has no data because it falls in a swath gap
claims.basis: Asserted before the mask was read. Pair A does hold values there, all flagged by the product's mask. The raw mask (13 Nov) gives value 10 on all 307 frame-74 pixels: no valid subswath in the 28 Aug acquisition. So the coverage gap turned out to be real, but 'has no data' was wrong and the cause was stated unchecked
claims.resolution: Withdrawn 13 Nov; superseded by C26, which states what the mask shows
forbidden: because it falls in a swath gap
which fall in a swath gap

claims.claim: At the source, a surface change was visible on 66% and movement measurable on 0%
claims.basis: Observability version 1 ignored the product's masks (S1)
claims.resolution: Recomputed 13 Nov with version 2: 0% usable for both tasks, 100% no valid data in the product. Version 1 figures stay withheld (observabilityCurrent, tested in finding.test.ts and observability.test.ts)
forbidden: a surface change was visible on
a surface change could be seen on

claims.claim: Mudflow coherence fell from 0.38 to 0.19 across the event while nearby ground went from 0.40 to 0.50
claims.basis: prepare_control_series.py on the raw files (13 Nov), median of valid pixels with block-bootstrap 95% intervals; across the event the intervals do not overlap (0.172 to 0.217 against 0.485 to 0.513). The pairs differ in length (24 and 12 days) and radar mode (4000 and 2000)
claims.action: Show with the confounds and 'does not establish the cause'; a like-for-like pair is the next test
claims.resolution: 13 Nov: replaces the earlier script's 0.41 to 0.28 and 0.42 to 0.52

claims.claim: The drop is specific to the mudflow, not the season
claims.basis: Causal attribution from one comparison
claims.resolution: Withdrawn 12 Nov: 'consistent with surface change in the mapped area; it does not establish the cause'
forbidden: specific to the mudflow, not the season

claims.claim: NISAR saw the Rasuwa mudflow change the ground
claims.basis: As C06
claims.resolution: Withdrawn 12 Nov: the headline now reports that coherence fell inside the mapped area
forbidden: saw the Rasuwa mudflow change the ground

claims.claim: Pair B correlation peak 0.18 at the source against 0.63 nearby
claims.basis: pair-b-analysis.json, frame 16: the peak is valid on all 307 source pixels; 60% of range offsets there are flagged or masked

claims.claim: Removing the ionosphere screen cuts phase scatter from 8.87 to 4.79 and from 6.41 to 1.98 rad
claims.basis: Whole-frame standard deviation across components; the sign is chosen empirically

claims.claim: Pixel offsets show no large coherent shift
claims.basis: GOFF layer 3, which has the smallest search window; raw values reach about 280 m
claims.action: The search-window limit is now stated in the story, README and SCIENTIFIC_VALIDATION

claims.claim: No displacement is calculated
claims.basis: True since 12 Nov: Tsho Rolpa movement bounds are research output only; no displacement layer exists (App.test.tsx)

claims.claim: The Tsho Rolpa dam moved less than about 2 cm, with no sign that it is slumping
claims.basis: S5: phase converted to centimetres without a confirmed convention or reference
forbidden: no sign that it is slumping

claims.claim: The glacier moved less than about 0.2 m in 12 days, or roughly 6 m a year
claims.basis: A 12-day bound extrapolated to a year

claims.claim: Tsho Rolpa measured 1.59 to 1.62 km², no change beyond about ±0.09 km²
claims.basis: Four GCOV dates, same track and frame; the ±0.09 km² is half the largest change between the −8 and −6 dB thresholds
claims.action: Called a method range, not a formal error (13 Nov)

claims.claim: The lake area matches published figures
claims.basis: About 1.55 km² (2008 survey), 1.61 km² (Peppa et al., 2020, ISPRS Annals V-3-2020) and 1.65 km² (2022 DHM bathymetric survey, as reported by Dialogue Earth)
claims.action: Cited 13 Nov. Obtain the DHM survey report itself

claims.claim: Dam-break arrival times and depths along 107 km
claims.basis: Assumed breach depths of 10, 20 and 30 m; the NISAR lake-area range (1.495 to 1.691 km²) carried through; peak-flow formulas differ about tenfold; no attenuation downstream, and the front moves at the water speed rather than the faster wave speed, two errors that pull the times in opposite directions. Every cross-section is published (data/qa, docs/SCENARIO_WORKING.md)
claims.action: Move out of the primary demonstration

claims.claim: Next: a forecast of the lake's size in 2030 and 2040
claims.basis: No method or long series

claims.claim: Terrain screen: 56% of the detachment zone High or Very high, AUC 0.66
claims.basis: One event; every unmapped pixel treated as a negative; neighbouring pixels not independent (S10)
claims.action: Called a one-event consistency check, not a validation, in the manifest, status registry and docs (13 Nov)

claims.claim: Roads: 73.3 km High exposure; 28.2 of 153.4 km could not be watched from Track 48, 4.8 km counting Track 98 too
claims.basis: Rule thresholds are project choices; the radar-watch rating uses the version 2 flags over frames 74 and 75; the either-direction share adds Track 98 frame 16 (13 Nov), counted per cell, never merging reasons
claims.resolution: 13 Nov: before frame 75 was assessed, 109 km lay beyond the frame checked

claims.claim: What-if flood: places below the water
claims.basis: Height above the nearest river point only. Every counted feature with its km and height is published (data/qa/rasuwa-2026-simulation-features.csv, docs/SCENARIO_WORKING.md)
claims.action: Move out of the primary demonstration

claims.claim: "Best supported" explanation
claims.basis: A rule count that could rise without a measurement (S7)
claims.resolution: Fixed 12 Nov: only radar values at the spot and independent mapping count; labels are Fits the checks, Partly fits, Little support

claims.claim: Runs offline from one click
claims.basis: 13 Nov: CascadeLens.zip built, unzipped fresh and started with its own serve.py (what the .bat runs); all 20 real-data browser tests passed against it under the offline CSP. The .bat itself was not run: no Windows machine here
claims.action: Run Start CascadeLens.bat once on Windows from a fresh unzip

claims.claim: Product maturity Provisional (P05023), read from the file DOI
claims.basis: manifest.maturity()

claims.claim: UNOSAT mudflow extent 64.91 km²
claims.basis: Computed in UTM 45N; press figures of about 30 km² are not reconciled

claims.claim: Following Earth's movement, one radar observation at a time
claims.basis: No movement is measured anywhere in the app
claims.resolution: Rephrased 13 Nov: 'Following change on Earth's surface'

claims.claim: At the source, Pair A holds no usable measurement: the product's mask marks no valid subswath in the 28 Aug acquisition
claims.basis: Raw unwrappedInterferogram/mask of the frame-74 event GUNW, read as the 32-bit P05023 field: all 307 detachment-zone pixels have low byte 10 (water 0, reference subswath 1, secondary subswath 0). Phase, components and coherence share the mask

claims.claim: From the opposite side (Track 98), coherence at the source is very low: median 0.09 against 0.46 near the channel
claims.basis: data/qa/pair-b-analysis.json, frame 16, valid-mask pixels: 100% of the 307 detachment-zone pixels valid. 28% of the zone is hidden by layover and 37% was already incoherent before the event, so low coherence there is not all change
claims.action: Always with 'other causes possible' (steep slopes, snow, a 12-day gap)

claims.claim: From Track 98, with every pair in one radar mode, the mudflow gap also opens across the event: 0.31 against 0.40 before, 0.13 against 0.49 across
claims.basis: prepare_control_series.py --view t98 on five frame 16 pairs, block-bootstrap 95% intervals. The pre-event pair is still 24 days against 12, and the control ground also falls by early October
claims.action: Consistent with surface change; does not establish the cause

claims.claim: A rainfall event-duration threshold (IMERG Late, BIPAD reports) did not beat chance for the corridor in 2025-2026: CSI 0.20 against a chance 95th percentile of 0.21, p = 0.12
claims.basis: run_rain_thresholds.py: fitted 2016-2022, calibrated 2023-2024, scored 2025-2026 with the 14 h publication delay; criterion stated in the script before scoring; month-preserving shuffle for chance
claims.action: Show with its qualifications: reports, not landslides; ward reference points; one run; BIPAD licence not established

claims.claim: CascadeLens warns of, or forecasts, rainfall-triggered landslides
claims.basis: The only landslide model run on real data (L2) missed its criterion (C29), and the readiness engine holds every landslide capability below Experimental
claims.resolution: Not claimed anywhere; kept as a guard for future wording

claims.claim: Cliff impact: candidate places where a flow could have hit a valley wall hard
claims.basis: A mentor, oral communication, no location or figures given. Bends and walls from the 30 m Copernicus DEM (not yet rebuilt on NASADEM), superelevation and run-up from the preliminary UNOSAT extent, with a straight-stretch control; no site stands out clearly. It does not confirm that an impact happened
claims.action: Keep out of the primary demonstration

claims.claim: The Rasuwa terrain on the map and in the 3D model is NASA's NASADEM
claims.basis: prepare_nasa_rasuwa.py mosaics the four NASADEM_HGT v001 tiles n27e084 to n28e085 (1 arc-second, EGM96). SRTM, February 2000: pre-event, gap-filled from other models on the steepest walls. The terrain screen, cliff-impact sites and What-if flood still use the Copernicus DEM, and Tsho Rolpa lies outside the NASADEM tiles downloaded
claims.action: Keep; rebuild the terrain screen, cliff sites and What-if flood on NASADEM before saying all Rasuwa terrain is NASA's

claims.claim: Real NISAR GCOV backscatter for Rasuwa is loaded: Track 48 on 16 and 28 August, Track 149 on 23 August and Track 98 on 12 September
claims.basis: Frequency A HHHH from each file, mask values 0 and 255 left out, averaged in linear power to 40 m (map) and 80 m (inspector). Frame 74 only for Tracks 48 and 149, so they cover 39 to 63% of the case area; Track 98 frame 16 covers 100%. Provisional, DOI 10.5067/NIL2GCOV-P1, CRID P05023. The catalogued 31 August Track 98 snapshot was not downloaded

claims.claim: NISAR backscatter on Track 48 changed by more than 3 dB on 27% of the mapped mudflow between 16 and 28 August, against 9.5% in the ground around it
claims.basis: data/qa/rasuwa-2026-backscatter-change.json: valid pixels only, 33% of the UNOSAT extent (frame 74 only); ring 1 km wide. Radar modes differ (40 and 20 MHz). Only one pair on this track, so no before-event control. UNOSAT's extent is preliminary
claims.action: Always with the valid share, the mode difference and 'does not establish the cause'

claims.claim: NASA OPERA Sentinel-1 images show the same pattern: more than 3 dB change on 23 to 24% of the mapped mudflow across the event, against 6% in the 12 days before and 5 to 6% in the ground around it
claims.basis: data/qa/rasuwa-2026-backscatter-change.json: OPERA RTC-S1 v1.0 VV, layover and shadow masked, 87 to 89% of the extent valid. Track 19 (descending) 12-24 Aug before, 24 Aug-5 Sep across; track 85 (ascending) 16-28 Aug across, 15% in the pair after. Sentinel-1 is an ESA mission processed by NASA JPL: not a NISAR result. Monsoon soil moisture also changes C-band backscatter
claims.action: Show with the control pair and 'consistent with surface change; does not establish the cause'
